probability.title: Probability
probability.goal: Be fluent with conditional probability and expectation

exam.format: Written, 2 hours, Thursday 19 November 2026; a mid-course exam on discrete probability only.
exam.coverage: Chapter 1, Chapter 3, Section 4.1 (discrete conditional probability, Bayes' formula and independence), Section 5.1 (important discrete distributions) and Sections 6.1–6.2 (expected value and variance of discrete random variables). It leaves out continuous densities (Chapter 2, Sections 4.2, 5.2, 6.3), covariance and correlation, and Chapters 7–9, which the end-of-term exam covers.

discrete-distributions.title: Discrete probability and the uniform distribution
discrete-distributions.question: How do we assign probabilities to the outcomes of a chance experiment with countably many outcomes?
discrete-distributions.purpose: Describe a discrete chance experiment by a distribution and find the probability of any event in it.

combinatorics.question: How do we count outcomes to find probabilities when the sample space is too large to list?
combinatorics.purpose: Find probabilities by counting the ways outcomes can occur.

discrete-conditional.question: How does learning that one event occurred change the probability of another?
discrete-conditional.purpose: Compute the probability of an event given that another occurred, including recognising when the condition changes nothing.

important-distributions.title: Important distributions
important-distributions.question: Which standard discrete distribution fits a given counting experiment?
important-distributions.purpose: Recognise which important distribution an experiment follows and compute its probabilities.

expected-value-variance.title: Expected value and variance
expected-value-variance.question: What can expected values tell us about discrete random variables?
expected-value-variance.purpose: Reason about discrete random variables through their expected values and variances.

refs.locator: §6.1 Expected Value; §6.2 Variance of Discrete Random Variables

continuous-densities.title: Continuous probability densities
continuous-densities.question: How do we assign probabilities when the outcomes fill a continuum?
continuous-densities.purpose: Describe a continuous experiment by a density and find probabilities as areas.

further-conditional.title: Paradoxes and continuous conditioning
further-conditional.question: How does conditioning behave beyond the simple discrete cases?
further-conditional.purpose: Apply conditional probability correctly to continuous outcomes and to puzzles where intuition misleads.

important-densities.title: Important densities and their simulation
important-densities.question: Which standard density fits a given continuous experiment?
important-densities.purpose: Recognise the important densities and compute or simulate probabilities from them.

continuous-expectation-covariance.title: Continuous random variables and covariance

continuous-expectation-covariance.purpose: Compute expected values, variances and covariances beyond a single discrete random variable.

sums-of-rvs.title: Sums of random variables
sums-of-rvs.question: What is the distribution of a sum of independent random variables?
sums-of-rvs.purpose: Find the distribution or density of a sum of independent random variables by convolution.

law-of-large-numbers.title: Law of large numbers
law-of-large-numbers.question: Why does the average of many independent trials settle near the expected value?
law-of-large-numbers.purpose: Bound how far an average of independent trials strays from its expected value.

real-analysis.title: Real Analysis
real-analysis.goal: Write rigorous epsilon-delta proofs before next term's course

exam.format: The lectures' entry test: written, 3 hours, five proofs, on Monday 8 February 2027.
exam.coverage: Chapters 1 to 3: the real numbers, sequences and series, and continuous functions.

basic-set-theory.title: Basic set theory
basic-set-theory.question: Which facts about sets, functions and counting do analysis proofs rest on?
basic-set-theory.purpose: Write the proofs about sets, functions and their sizes that every later argument in analysis relies on.

real-numbers.title: Real numbers
real-numbers.question: What property of $\mathbb{R}$ makes analysis possible where $\mathbb{Q}$ fails?
real-numbers.purpose: Prove facts about real numbers from the axioms of an ordered field with the least-upper-bound property.

sequences-limits.title: Sequences and their limits
sequences-limits.question: When does a sequence of real numbers converge?
sequences-limits.purpose: Prove facts about the convergence of sequences from the definition of the limit.

infinite-series.title: Series
infinite-series.question: When does an infinite sum of real numbers converge?
infinite-series.purpose: Decide and prove whether a series converges.

function-limits-continuity.title: Function limits and continuity
function-limits-continuity.question: What can epsilon-delta limits prove about functions of a real variable?
function-limits-continuity.purpose: Prove limits and continuity of functions with epsilon-delta arguments and use the theorems continuity gives.

differentiation.title: The derivative
differentiation.question: What does it mean for a function to be differentiable?
differentiation.purpose: Prove the rules of differentiation and the theorems built on the mean value theorem.

riemann-integral-arc.title: The Riemann integral
riemann-integral-arc.question: How is the integral of a function defined rigorously?
riemann-integral-arc.purpose: Build the Riemann integral rigorously and prove the results of calculus that rest on it.

sequences-of-functions.title: Sequences of functions
sequences-of-functions.question: How far do the ideas of limits reach beyond sequences of real numbers?
sequences-of-functions.purpose: Carry the ideas of limits beyond the real line, to sequences of functions and to metric spaces.
